highlights.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse gives out user’s home address without permission, sending buyer to his house
highlights.summary: The new AI agent, Muse, was released last week and has been downloaded by 3 million users. When Usman asked if a keyboard for sale on Facebook Marketplace was still available on Saturday, he received an enthusiastic and immediate response. “Yep still available!” wrote Matt Robb.
body: The two agreed on a price, and Robb sent his Toronto address. Usman, wife and daughter in tow, showed up several hours later at Robb’s home and sent a text that he had arrived.
Robb responded, “yep I’m here!”, but he was not at home. Nobody walked out of the apartment building.

Usman sent Robb a picture of the building’s door and wrote, “Hello???? I am standing outside.” After 20 minutes of no face-to-face contact, he abandoned the sale. “Man if you didn’t want to sell it why did you waste my time man,” he wrote, and drove away.
An hour later, Robb, or who Usman thought was Robb, responded apologetically. “Hey really sorry about tonight, got tied up and missed you completely,” read the message, which the Guardian reviewed.

highlights.title: GTA 6’s $400 Collector’s Edition Is the Latest Example of a Horrible Trend
highlights.summary: Spendy deluxe editions are nothing new in the world of video games. For many years now, players have had the option to pay a bit more than retail price — often between $20 and $50 extra — for a bundle of extra goodies to enhance a new game they're looking forward to playing.
body: Last week, Rockstar revealed its Goodtime State – Vice City Collection collectors box for GTA 6, a $400 assortment of branded merch that does not include a copy of the game. It's the latest example of how the industry has pivoted to pursuing high-spending players instead of trying to reach a wider audience.

Back when Sony announced plans to stop producing physical games industry analyst Mat Piscatella pointed out the writing on the wall. "In a world where consoles potentially cost $1k+ the focus shifts from trying to attract the mass market to targeting only the most affluent with the least price sensitivity and highest preference for convenience," he wrote in a July 3 post on Bluesky. If you zoom out a bit, you can see that same strategy at play when it comes to collector's editions, too.

The film, which premiered to much fanfare at the Toronto International Film Festival earlier this month, follows the making of 1976’s Rocky, with Anthony Ippolito playing a young version of Stallone as he develops and pushes the film through a tumultuous production.

The star emphasized he has “nothing to do” with the movie, which was directed by Peter Farrelly. “I said, ‘I’ll just sit back and watch.’ I talked to the kid. I said, ‘If you want any questions, here I am,’ and that was it. But they did it all on their own,” as Stallone joked that in seeing Ippolito’s portrayal, “I go, ‘Do I talk like that?’ Now I get it. Now I get it.”

Elsewhere in the conversation, Stallone spoke about what it’s like for him to watch the Rocky movies now (“It’s like you look at a photo of yourself, everyone else likes it, but you go [growl]”) and revealed he’s trying to get Amazon to let him recut 1990’s Rocky V, calling the movie “a thorn in my side.”

highlights.title: AI is supercharging hacking, and your local hospitals and banks aren’t ready
highlights.summary: In March, Janice Malone began getting calls about suspicious activity from her nonprofit organization, Vivian's Door. Vivian's Door, headquartered in Alabama, typically provided training, resources, and community to underserved and minority-owned businesses.
body: New models are helping Big Tech shore up its cyber defenses. What about everyone else?

The organization’s third-party IT team pulled its systems offline for three days while they investigated the issue and plugged up the vulnerability, leaving Malone with a bill of about $3,000. She feared that she’d exposed information about the companies she was trying to help. Even more ominously, she wasn’t completely sure if the attack was engineered by a human hacker or helped along by an AI system, or whether more were on the way.

The past months have seen AI revolutionize the field of cybersecurity. OpenAI and Anthropic have disclosed that “rogue” systems escaped restrictions in their own labs and hacked everything from a small German wiki to the Australian government. Even before that, powerful models like Anthropic’s Mythos created an arms race to advance AI cybersecurity, and even lighter-weight models have allowed human bad actors to supercharge their hacking efforts.

highlights.summary: The Elder Scrolls never got a Fallout: New Vegas -like spinoff because Todd Howard is "very protective" of the IP, according to former Bethesda developer Kurt Kuhlmann.
body: Kuhlmann, who served as lead designer and senior designer at the Microsoft studio for 20 years before leaving in 2023, shared details on his experience working on the legendary fantasy RPG franchise during an interview with FRVR. Fans have spent decades wondering why The Elder Scrolls never got the same spinoff treatment as Fallout has, but he said there's a pretty specific reason why that's the case.

"The whole New Vegas thing did create this, at least the perception of this, 'Who makes a better Fallout game? Oh, they should just give it to Obsidian’," Kuhlmann said. "There are the Obsidian, the New Vegas people, that think obviously New Vegas is way better, Obsidian is way better at making those games, and why don’t they just get Fallout altogether?"
Kuhlmann isn't sure "that Todd wanted to create that situation again for The Elder Scrolls." He added, "Todd, from my time there, he is very protective of it."

highlights.summary: NASA announced on Monday that it will exercise options to purchase two additional flights on Boeing's Starliner spacecraft, as well as financially support the company in its efforts to return the crewed vehicle to flight and find a new rocket after the Atlas V vehicle retires.
body: The space agency’s announcement confirms reporting by Ars Technica earlier this month on NASA’s plans to maintain access to low-Earth orbit after the impending retirement of SpaceX’s Crew Dragon vehicle.

“I do not think it’s a secret that SpaceX intends to sunset older platforms like Falcon and Dragon as they concentrate on their next-generation capability, Starship,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said during a news conference on Monday afternoon.

Dragon has successfully been flying NASA astronauts into orbit for more than six years. Boeing, by contrast, has struggled mightily to bring the Starliner vehicle into service for NASA. Starliner experienced numerous issues on uncrewed test flights in 2019 and 2022; most seriously, thruster issues nearly led to the catastrophic loss of two astronauts during the spacecraft’s first crew test flight in June 2024.

highlights.title: When can we say AI made a scientific discovery?
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Last Wednesday, Anthropic announced that earlier this year it had launched a molecular biology lab, where Claude agents read and conjecture about hard biology…
body: To understand what Anthropic says its system did, imagine you’re flipping through a library of millions of DNA sequences, amassed as scientists sequence more and more of the living world. One step toward a breakthrough might be finding a peculiar sequence that encodes an interesting enzyme, perhaps. Then you’d need to figure out what that enzyme does and, eventually, how to manipulate it to do something useful.

What Anthropic says its system of 950 agents found after 21 hours was not a brand-new sequence. The agents instead flagged a repeating pattern surrounding a known enzyme, a particular pattern Anthropic said hadn’t been catalogued before. But if you read through Anthropic’s announcement, which calls this pattern “reminiscent” of what led to the gene-editing technology CRISPR that “has already transformed science and medicine,” it sounds as if this army of agents really found something of note.

body: Over the weekend, Toby Morton spent time updating his latest and perhaps most controversial website, which names and posts a threat to the seven men named in a civil rape case filed two weeks ago in New York that has grabbed the nation and led to outcry about sexual assault over the past few days.

The simple website contains a page that names the seven defendants in Jane Doe’s suit and contains blank boxes that indicate that photos of them will be uploaded —and potentially pages for the men who are facing accusations.

“The [website] will bring together her account, the lawsuit, public records, documented reporting, institutional responses and additional verified information as it becomes available,” Morton wrote on the site. “The goal is not to be first. The goal is to build a record that can withstand scrutiny. This will take time. I will be careful. It will be documented.”

Morton wrote that as new photos and information are shared, he’ll be including members of the Cornell administration who he said “failed miserably.” He also anticipated that he’d be conflated with a journalist investigating the men accused of assaulting the young woman while students at Cornell.

highlights.title: ‘It’s such a joy to ride:’ this cargo e-bike makes errands and commuting a breeze
highlights.summary: This pricey ebike is a gamechanger for going around town, getting groceries and hauling cargo with ease – without paying for gas. The best bike lights and bike locks in the US. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Parking a car in an urban area can be stressful. Spaces are often hard to find, traffic congestion is a pain and it just takes extra time.

An electric bike changes that paradigm – you can roll up on the curb, lock your bike, and walk to your destination. Recently, I tested the Lectric XPedition2, an electric cargo bike that not only made grocery shopping easier but helped me explore my city stress-free.

Like the competing Aventon Abound and Specialized Haul, the XPedition2 is an electric bike meant to haul cargo. But this one only comes as a long-tail, meaning it has an extended rack on the back for transporting library books, groceries and even little kids.

The Lectric XPedition2 costs $1,399 which is admittedly much more expensive than an entry-level non-electric bike. Yet, it’s such a joy to ride, so stable and balanced, and lasts so long on a charge that I’ve started driving far less, especially in a downtown area. My daily errands such as coffee runs and shopping are less stressful and more enjoyable.

body: The deal is expected to close by the end of the year. Li will become EVP and chief scientist at AMD, reporting to AMD CEO Lisa Su, while the World Labs team will “continue to focus on advancing AI model research.” AMD also notes that the acquisition will strengthen “its ability to develop AI hardware, software and systems around the needs of emerging models and applications.”

“Just like I knew it was time to do a startup to jumpstart the work of creating foundation models beyond LLMs and achieve the most impact in AI, it’s again very clear that the right path for myself and World Labs is to continue our mission as a part of AMD,” Li says in a post on her Substack. “Together we’re committed to keep pushing the frontier of AI to solve real problems, and doing so openly with the community and the entire ecosystem.”

body: The world No 1 was aiming to bounce back from his quarter-final exit to Jonny Clayton in the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam a week ago. Littler threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the event, and missed the latest Players Championship events in Den Bosch.

Playing in front of a more supportive crowd in Leicester on Monday, Littler raced out of the blocks in the double-in, double-out format, taking the opening leg while Woodhouse was still in the 300s. “The Nuke” then hit a double 15 to complete a 106 checkout as he won the first set 3-1 despite looking far from his best.

Woodhouse took the lead for the first time in the second set, the world No 18 from Worcestershire roaring 2-1 ahead in legs. Even when Littler levelled at 2-2, Woodhouse held his nerve on a double 16 in the decider to set up a deciding set.

highlights.title: The SaaSpocalypse that wasn’t, with Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Mike Cannon-Brookes, who is cofounder and CEO of Atlassian. Atlassian is one of those companies that every other company runs on — it makes important platform tools like Jira and Trello that allow people to organize and manage big teams, create shared databases of company…
body: Mike Cannon-Brookes on AI in the enterprise, Atlassian’s new org chart, and why chatbots aren’t the future of work.

All of this means Atlassian is also right in the middle of the way AI is changing how all these companies work — AI tools might be able to look at all the different tools and systems you have and just read them for you, making a big migration to Atlassian’s platform less enticing. Or, if you buy the idea of the so-called SaaSpocalypse, AI might just build all of these tools for you, destroying this entire category of businesses.

Obviously, Mike had a lot of thoughts pushing back on this. So we spent some real time talking about the value of design, human users, how AI is actually increasing the usage of Atlassian’s tools, and what this all looks like a few years from now.

Of course, AI has also changed Atlassian. Like so many other tech companies, Atlassian did a round of layoffs earlier this year, with Mike saying he felt the company needed a different “mix of skills.” So I asked Mike what he thinks that mix of skills is and how AI is changing what it means to run a software company.

highlights.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Is Reportedly Already Planning a Re-Release With New Footage
highlights.summary: Deadline has reported that Sony is preparing a new cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which will be released into theaters in the future. There's currently no word on when this re-release will drop, but the window for it to happen this year is rapidly shrinking as the holiday season approaches.
body: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is reportedly already planning a re-release, which will feature new footage.

This isn't the first time Sony has done this for the webhead. In 2022, the company re-released Spider-Man: No Way Home with additional footage, including extended scenes featuring all three Spider-Men. Admittedly, it wasn't anything to write home about, and it was arguably a worse movie due to how these extra scenes disrupted its overall pacing. It added about 10 extra minutes to the original film, so it's possible something similar will happen here with Brand New Day.

Similarly, Avengers: Endgame is cleaning up at the box office seven years after its release thanks to a new re-release, which adds newly-shot footage that connects it to Avengers: Doomsday. All of these re-releases seem to be done with at least a partial goal of boosting the film's box office numbers; Brand New Day is currently the number one film at the domestic box office, and third globally. Avengers: Endgame's re-release is allowing it to quickly close the gap between it and the number one film, Avatar.
points: Deadline has reported that Sony is preparing a new cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which will be released into theaters in the future.

highlights.title: ‘12 weeks and SO disgusted by my dog’: what happens when you’re pregnant and can’t stand your pet?
highlights.summary: There may be almost no research on pet aversion during and post-pregnancy, but it may not be particularly rare. About three weeks into her first pregnancy, Sylvia Luu began to loathe the smell of her border collie mix, Ranger.
body: Luu could hardly be in the same room as Ranger without becoming nauseous. His drool repulsed her, and she found the smell of his fur so disgusting she wore a nose plug all day.
“Before pregnancy, I used to smell my dog’s paws a lot,” says Luu. “But during pregnancy, I would throw up if I ever tried that.”
At the time, Luu, 35, and Ranger had enjoyed 12 happy years together. Ranger slept in Luu’s bed. She walked him in all weather, and let him lick her face.

Luu’s doctor said that her nausea was normal and simply advised her to drink more water to avoid dehydration from vomiting, but that didn’t alleviate Luu’s distress. “I was so heartbroken that I couldn’t love my dog as much as I wanted to,” says Luu, whose husband took over pet care duties. She wondered about rehoming Ranger, and was relieved when, upon delivering her firstborn, her aversion vanished.

“I just want Billy to enjoy his football with a smile. If he can do that, the rest will come. I remember him well when he was in Brighton. I thought he was fantastic for them.”
